notes.title: Mohrta is now one of my must-plays for 2025: A surreal, striking FPS that somehow got soulslike levels and bosses working on the Doom engine
notes.notes: Doom engine FPS-RPG-soulslike thing Mohrta has gotten a new trailer highlighting its strange world and 2025 release window as part of The PC Gaming Show: Most Wanted, but you don't have to wait until next year to check this one out⁠—I spent nearly three hours playing Mohrta's generous demo on Steam, and it got me giddy for the full deal even with the glut of boomer shooters in recent years... Read more.

notes.title: Mohrta Demo Update
notes.notes:
Hello everyone, I hope you backed up your builds to continue your current save, because the new Mohrta Demo update is out! Featuring a million bug fixes, new features, and quality of life stuff.

Things that were addressed will be listed below, but I want to extend a huge thank you to both Bridgeburner of Hellforge Studios, and Sanya of Waffle Iron Studios for their enormous help in solving the .ini issues that were plaguing the previous build. Thank you both so, so much!

Now, as for fixes:

[b]New Features:[/b]
-Completely redone Lantern Beast “Van”. Now acts as a traditional flashlight.
-Images display when interacting with tutorials of any kind.
-More details added to Kozanoda, improved collisions and hitboxes.
-Joypad controls, including an experimental “Lock-On” feature, available only to joypad users.
-Additional Strange Ore to incentivize upgrading weapons.

[b]Bug Fixes:[/b]
-Fixed ini issue, so now everyone will start with the proper keybindings, visuals, HUD display.
-This also allowed for the Dodge action to be bound to shift, as originally intended. Please give your pinkies my apologies.
-Reduced the HP of Kozanoda’s boss, Igoro.
-Added collisions to objects in Kozanoda that did not have them.
-Blocked off the player from accessing the rooftops of Kozanoda’s glitchy buildings.
-Replaced the TNT barrels in Igoro’s boss arena with normal barrels (the implication was that he ate the TNT in the barrels, but no one got it… my bad… my bad…)
-Fixed the Black Screen problem in 1-1
-Fixed both errors with Juli’s cutscenes being skipped, causing the bars to not go down or back up.
-Fixed Ru’uk’s questline bugs.
-Adjusted placements of some props to look better.
-Fixed many instances of softlocking due to falling between props.
-Fixed misplaced character at the beginning of the Metro nexus.
-Fixed a softlock when trying to talk to a character behind the right-most bar in Metronexus.
-Fixed a softlock where you would get into an infinite chatting loop with Ru’uk’s ghost in 1-3.


Thanks for playing the demo! And thanks for bearing with us while we figured all this crap out. We want to do this right, and this demo was extremely important for us to catch things we would have otherwise missed.

[i]Godspeed, Hayward

-Scumhead[/i]

notes.title: Mohrta Demo Troubleshooting
notes.notes:
Hello all, thanks for playing the Mohrta Demo!

Before we begin, I recommend backing up your Mohrta game files to somewhere else on your PC, GZDoom updates erase save data, so if you want to continue to play your current save- please back up your build within the next few days before I launch the new update.

Other than that, I wanted to take some time here to elaborate on some technical issues we’ve run into.

Some people have been running into issues such as incorrect lighting, strange keybindings, missing HUD, and more. These are all issues with the way GZDoom handles the .ini file. The easiest way to fix this would be uninstalling Mohrta, deleting the .ini file in Documents/MyGames/Gzdoom, and then reinstalling Mohrta. This should get you on the proper settings. If you don’t want to do this, I will go through some settings, and what they should be set to.

Before listing, you can find all of these settings by using the ‘option search’ button, or the “Full Options Menu” button in GZDoom.

[b]Also, do not press reset to defaults in the options menu, this will undo a ton of changes I made to the .ini to make Mohrta look how it does. Sorry![/b]

[b][i]My game is too bright and/or uglier than the screenshots![/i][/b]

Make sure Gamma and brightness are lower than the default.
Brightness: -0.05
Gamma: 0.94
Bloom Lighting: ON
Ambient Occlusion: Low
Sector Light Mode: Dark
Texture Filtering Mode: None

[i][b]My HUD is missing, I don’t have a cross-hair![/b][/i]

Try using the + and - keys to resize your hud. If that doesn’t work, there’s a setting in Display options called Screen Size that you can adjust to show the HUD. Setting this to 10 instead of 11 should help.

As for the crosshair, Mohrta’s current build does not include one, but you can enable it in the options settings if you’d like.

[i][b]My controls are all wrong! My settings aren’t saving![/b][/i]

This is a new issue that we’ve run into and are working on. For the time being, try deleting your documents .ini and restarting mohrta to see if that helps it. This is something we may need help with, so if you’ve found a solution, please comment below.

[i][b]Why are there key binds that don’t seem to do anything? I can’t crouch?[/b][/i]

You’d be right, you can’t crouch. GZDoom is a strange beast- there aren't many keybinds we can use so we had to dip into things like Zoom and Crouch for certain button actions. If you want to rebind your dodge, please use the menu that references the player actions directly. If that doesn’t work, you could try to edit your .ini file directly, either the documents one or the one inside the Mohrta game folder.

[i][b]Where can I find what inventory items I have? (Ore, Mana Crystals, etc.)[/b][/i]

This is currently a work in progress, and will be available in the finished game.

[i][b]I’m stuck in the level terrain![/b][/i]

All cheats are enabled in this Mohrta Demo, the same ones that can be found in any gzdoom project. You can use Noclip to free yourself or skip past any bugs you might come across. There’s a lot we didn’t run into during our limited testing period, so please bear with us as we fix these things we missed.

[i][b]The Camera movement is nauseating![/b][/i]

Go to options > full options menu > tilt++

From there, you can adjust camera movement and intensity however you like.


[i][b]If you have any other questions, please comment.[/b][/i]

Oh and if you want to screw around with some of the weaponry not included in the demo, try typing “pukename inventory_test” in the console, heheh.
